[P1] 宋江杀惜
水浒
之八
出版说明
《水浒》是我国的一部古典文学名著。为了满足
广大读者的需要，我们把它编绘成连环画册。在编绘
上尽量保持原著故事情节，但是为了适合用连环画来
表现，个别情节也作了一些删节和改动。
全部画册分为三十集，每集有比较完整的故事，
可以独自成章；同时，每集内容上下衔接，以便连续
阅读。为了阅读方便，每集开头写有内容提要，结尾
附有后记，用以交代上集、本集和下集故事大意。
《水浒》连环画，我社1956——1962年陆续出版
过。现在这套连环画，是用原有的文学脚本重新绘制
的。
№ 000152

宋江杀惜
（《水浒》之八）

高适 绘

人民美术出版社

[P3] 内容提要
上集《石碣村》说的是：晁盖等七个好汉智取生辰纲事发，被官府缉拿，幸得宋江事先告知，避走石碣村。官兵追至，众好汉将官兵统统打死，然后投奔梁山；王伦不肯收留，林冲怒杀王伦，晁盖做了梁山寨主。
本集故事紧接上集：梁山派刘唐送金子和书信给宋江。宋江一时疏忽，将放金子和书信的招文袋遗落在阎婆惜处。阎婆惜发现宋江私通梁山，抓住把柄，趁机要挟。宋江怒杀阎婆惜，逃往沧州。
1 济州官兵两次被梁山好汉打败，蔡京大怒，撤换了知府。新知府上任之后，招兵买马，集草屯粮，又下公文到附近州县，相约对付梁山。

[P4] 2 济州府所属郓城县得了济州公文，知县忙唤押司宋江写成文案，通知各村。宋江看了公文，心里寻思：晁盖等众人，不想做下这般大事，犯了大罪。虽是被人逼迫，于法度上却饶不得。倘有疏失，如之奈何！
3 宋江从衙内出来，走到街上，只听后面有人叫“押司”，回头看时，却见做媒的王婆，引着一个婆子，向着他指指点点地说话。
你有缘，做好事的押司来了！

[P5] 望押司慈悲，
施一具棺材！
4 王婆拉着那婆子来见宋江。那婆子姓阎，东京人氏。
一家三口，到山东投亲不遇，流落在此，只靠女儿卖唱
为生。昨天她老伴害时疫死了，无钱安葬，正走投无路
……
多谢押司大恩！
5 宋江答应施一具棺材。当下去酒店借笔砚写了张帖子叫她们到县东陈三郎家去取；又给了婆子十两银子，
备办后事。

[P6] 6 过了几天，阎婆来向宋江道谢，见他房里没有女人，便向隔壁王婆探问宋江可有家室。王婆说没有，阎婆便告诉王婆，想把女儿婆惜给宋江作个侧室。
7 王婆找宋江说了这事。宋江起初不肯，经不住王婆撺掇，也就依允了。

[P7] 8 宋江在县西巷内赁了一处楼房，买了些家具，安顿了阎婆惜娘儿两个，日子过得舒舒服服。只是宋江是个好汉，只爱学使枪棒，又因公务繁忙，不常来家，因此很不中那妇人的意。
9 一日，宋江请了他的同房押司张文远来阎婆家吃酒。这张文远是个酒色之徒，外号“小张三”，倒也生得俊俏，婆惜一见，便十分欢喜。两人眉来眼去，都有了意。

[P8] 10 从此张文远趁宋江不在家，便偷偷摸摸跑去，假意只说寻宋江。那妇人留住吃茶，两人言来语去，便勾搭上了。
11 他俩人明来暗去，打得火一般热。日子长了，街坊邻舍知道了，都在背后窃窃私议。

[P9] 12 虽然有些风声传到宋江耳朵里，但他肚里寻思：又不是自己结发之妻，何苦惹些闲气，以后不上她家门就是了。从此宋江有几个月没去。阎婆托人来请，宋江也推说有事。
13 一天傍晚，宋江从衙门出来，到对过茶坊里吃茶，忽见一个大汉，跨着一口朴刀，背着包袱，走得汗流满面，直向县衙里面看。

[P10] 14 宋江见那大汉来得蹊跷，忙跟了上去。他仔细一看，觉得有些面熟，却记不起在哪里见过。那大汉立住了脚看宋江，也有些认得。
15 那大汉去路边一个铺子里向掌柜的打听。掌柜的告诉他，这是宋押司。大汉便上前招呼，请宋江到个僻静地方去说话。

[P11] 16 宋江和那大汉到一家酒楼上一个僻静地方坐下。那大汉倚下朴刀，解下包裹，扔在桌子底下，扑身便拜。
17 宋江慌忙答礼。大汉说他便是赤发鬼刘唐，奉晁头领之命，特来面谢大恩人。宋江问起梁山情形，刘唐一一说了。

[P12] 你七人初到山寨，正缺银子使用，我家中还能过活，无需全留。
18 刘唐打开包裹，取出晁盖的信和一百两黄金交给宋江。宋江看完信，取了一条金子，和信一起放在招文袋内，剩下的金子叫刘唐带回去。
19 刘唐苦苦要宋江收下金子，宋江执意不肯，当下取笔砚给晁盖写了一封回信。刘唐只好将金子又包在包裹内。宋江便叫酒保拿酒肉与刘唐吃。

[P13] 兄弟保重，再
不可来，此间做公
的多，不是要处。
20 天色已晚，宋江怕出事，要刘唐连夜返回山寨。刘
唐告辞，宋江送到巷口，又拉住刘唐的手，叮嘱了几句。
押司哪里
去来？好两日
不见面。
21 刘唐走后，宋江走回下处。他边走边肚里寻思：幸
是做公的没看见，险些儿惹出一场大事来！转了两个弯，
只听背后有人叫他，回头看时，却又是阎婆。

[P14] 我儿，你的三郎来了！
23 宋江吃那婆子缠不过，只得跟她同到阎家。婆子把宋江拖进门，忙喊婆惜下楼来迎接。那妇人以为是张三来了，慌忙起身，用手掠掠头发，飞也似的跑下楼来。
24 婆惜从窗棂子里见是宋江，便又转了回去。婆子听见女儿又上楼去了，便对宋江说了些好话，硬拖他上楼去。

[P15] 25 宋江心里很不自在，因被婆子拖住，不能脱身，只得勉强走上楼来。那婆惜却躺在床上不肯起来。
26 宋江朝凳上坐了。阎婆拖起女儿，要她过来陪宋江。那妇人哪里肯，好歹朝宋江坐了，却别转了脸。
看你多么任性，平日用言语来伤触他，恼得押司不上门，你又想念他，这是何苦。

[P16] 27 阎婆一个人唠叨了半天，搭讪着要到街上去买些果品来下酒，便下楼去了。宋江想溜走，不料阎婆却从外面把门扣上了。
28 宋江无法，只得坐下来。不一会儿，阎婆端上酒来，说好说歹，大家才坐下吃酒。宋江也只得端起杯子，饮了三五杯……

[P17] 29 却说郓城县有个卖糟腌的唐牛儿，因为宋江时常济助他，每逢听到些公事就跑去告知宋江；宋江要用他时，他也决不推辞。这天他因赌钱输了，又去找宋江。
30 唐牛儿向街坊探听，知宋江到阎婆家去了。他跑到阎家，见门没关，便自进去；走到楼梯旁边，听见上面只有阎婆一人的说笑声。

[P18] 31 唐牛儿蹑手蹑脚，上了楼，悄悄往里看，见宋江和阎婆惜两个都低头无语。
32 唐牛儿闪身进来，对三人行了礼。宋江见他来，想谋个脱身之计，便向唐牛儿唠了唠嘴。唐牛儿瞧得明白，就瞎编了一番话，来骗阎婆。
敢莫是衙里有要案事？
正因早上那件公事，知县相公在厅上发作，正派四五个差人到处找你。

[P19] 句句都是实话，并不曾说谎。
你这贼精也来骗老娘，看你骗得过去？
33 宋江说：“这等要紧，只得去。”便起身要下楼。阎婆哪里肯依，说一定是唐牛儿撒谎骗她。唐牛儿和她争辩，阎婆就和他争吵起来……
你为什么打我？
你破人买卖衣饭，如杀人父母妻子！
34 两人越吵越凶，这婆子跳起身来，向唐牛儿劈脖子一叉，踉踉跄跄，直从房里叉下楼来。

[P20] 35 唐牛儿朝着阎婆钻过来，却被阎婆叉开五指，照脸上连打两掌，直跌到门外去了。阎婆把门关上，嘴里还直顾骂。
36 唐牛儿立在门外拍胸顿足，大骂着走了。
贼老咬虫，我不看宋押司面上，教你这屋粉碎！

[P21] 天色不早，
你两口儿早些
安歇了吧！
37 阎婆上了楼，在宋江面前又把唐牛儿骂了一阵，宋江越发无法脱身。那婆子又劝了几杯酒，便催宋江安歇。
38 宋江心想：今天晚了，走又走不脱，且看这妇人还有无情分。坐了一会，只见那妇人也不脱衣裳，便上床去扭身朝里面睡了。

[P22] 39 宋江寻思：可恨这贱人全不睬我！只好暂且睡一睡，明天一早就走。他从腰里解下系着招文袋和一把裁纸尖刀的鸾带挂在床栏杆上，便和那妇人背靠背睡了。
40 宋江心中气闷，哪里睡得着，好容易挨到五更，起来就盆里冷水洗了一把脸，走下楼来。

[P23] 押司请喝
碗热汤再走。
41 宋江走出阎家，一直要奔回下处来，从县衙前面经过，只见卖热面汤的王老汉在县前赶早市。那老汉叫住宋江，递了碗醒酒汤给他吃。
啊呀！
42 宋江端过汤来吃了几口，想起曾经许过这老汉一口棺材，眼前正好将晁盖送来的金子给他，便随手揭起前襟，想去拿那金子，这才发现不见了招文袋。

[P24] 43 宋江吃了一惊，心里暗想：这可糟了，那招文袋如被那女人拿了，发觉里面有晁盖的书信，如何是好。想罢立刻转回头，向阎婆家走去。
44 这边阎婆惜好不容易等宋江走了，想爬起来脱了衣服再睡，一抬头，看见床栏杆上那条紫罗鸾带，便顺手提了过来。

[P25] 好呀，宋江宋江，原来你私通梁山！今日撞在老娘手里了！
45 婆惜提起招文袋和刀子，觉得袋里沉甸甸地，便往床上一抖，抖出一包金子和一封书信。这妇人识得几个字，把书信在灯前看了看，就叫起好来。
46 婆惜心里高兴，将书信、金子和刀子一齐又装进招文袋。这时，楼下门响，她猜想一定是宋江回来了，便把鸾带和招文袋藏在被子里，盖上被假装睡觉。

[P26] 47 宋江走了进来，径去床头栏杆上取时，招文袋却不见了，不觉吃了一惊。
48 宋江只得忍了气，用手去摇那妇人，要那招文袋。阎婆惜只假做睡着了，并不作声。
大姐还我招文袋！

[P27] 这里又没人来，一定是你拿了。
49 宋江只得向妇人央告，那妇人还是不理；又再三问她，她却说没有看见。宋江急了，说一定是她藏起来了。
大姐不要喊叫，邻舍听见，不是耍处。
好哇，原来你私通梁山贼人！
50 那妇人听宋江说是她拿了，圆睁两眼说：“拿是拿了，就是不还。”说着便“梁山长、梁山短”地嚷了起来。宋江连忙求她不要嚷叫。

[P28] 51 宋江又央告了半天，婆惜说，若要讨回招文袋，必须依从三件事：第一，任凭她改嫁张三；第二，一切穿戴使用的都归她所有；第三，快拿出晁盖信上说的一百两金子，全数给她。
52 宋江说前两件事都依得，只是那金子他只收了十两，剩下的都由送信人带走了。那妇人哪里肯信。宋江没法，求她给他三天期限，把家私变卖一百两金子给她。

[P29] 53 那妇人却不答应，一定要一手交钱，一手交货，并说如果是那样的话，三天之后再来拿招文袋。宋江又苦苦央告，妇人恼了，说：‘今天如若拿不出金子，明天到公堂上去取招文袋！’
54 宋江听见‘公堂’二字，怒气直起，哪里按捺得住，便不顾一切，动手来扯那妇人的被。
你到底
还也不还？
到县衙
门还你！

[P30] 55 妇人也不顾被子，只紧紧抱住招文袋。宋江见招文袋就在妇人胸前，便上来抢夺。
56 妇人死也不放。宋江狠命一拉，拉出那把裁纸尖刀来，便一把握在手里。那妇人以为宋江要行凶，就拼命大叫起来。
黑三郎：要杀人了！

[P31] 57 宋江肚里的闷气正好没处发泄，经她这一喊，真个起了杀心。妇人却待叫第二声时，宋江按住她的脖子，手起刀落，把她杀了。
58 宋江杀了婆惜，连忙取过招文袋，抽出那封信，就灯下烧了。

[P32] 你女儿太无礼，被我杀了。
哪有这事？一定是押司说笑话。
59 宋江整一整衣服，便走下楼来。阎婆听见女儿叫喊，慌忙奔上楼，却好和宋江撞个满怀。宋江便向阎婆说明杀死婆惜之事。
60 阎婆还不相信，跑到房里一看，啊呀一声，只说押司杀了她女儿，教她怎么过活。宋江忙说不妨，由他赡养。

[P33] 61 阎婆装作依允了，只求宋江为她女儿办后事。宋江想写个字据要阎婆去陈三郎家取棺材，阎婆不肯，要和宋江一齐前去。宋江就和婆子一同出来……
62 此时天色才明，阎婆和宋江路过县衙门口。县衙大门刚开，婆子出其不意，一把扭住宋江，大声喊叫起来。
有杀人
贼在这里！

[P34] 婆子快放手，
有事好说，押司
不是这等人！
63 宋江慌了，待要拦住婆子，哪里拦得住。却早有几个公差走拢来看，见是宋江，便劝婆子放了宋江。原来宋江平日为人最好，上下敬爱，因此公差不信这婆子的话，不肯当场拿他。
老贼虫
你做什么扭
住押司？
64 恰巧这时唐牛儿来卖糟姜。他见阎婆扭住宋江喊叫，想起昨晚的一肚子怒气来，便上前一把把婆子的手拆开，又叉开五指，打了阎婆一个巴掌。宋江趁势走脱了。

[P35] 65 阎婆只得抓住唐牛儿喊叫。那三四个公差，刚才碍着宋江面皮，不肯动手；现在宋江一走，他们便上前把婆子和唐牛儿带到县衙门里去了。
66 知县升堂，阎婆告宋江杀死她女儿，并攀住唐牛儿，说他昨晚从中撺掇，今早又使凶手逃脱了。知县有心开脱宋江，便说宋江是诚实君子，怎肯杀人，这人命之事必然在唐牛儿身上。

[P36] 67 唐牛儿说他并不知杀死阎婆女儿的事。知县不理，叫当厅公吏取了各人供词，带领仵作、里正等来到阎婆家验尸身和凶器。证明死者确系被杀身死。
68 那知县有心要救宋江，只把唐牛儿来拷问，不容他申辩，叫公差将他捆翻重打，并叫取一面枷钉了，禁在牢里。
小人只是过路劝架，委实不知宋押司杀人之事。

[P37] 69 不料这文案落在张文远手里。他一心要替阎婆惜报仇，便拿着凶器，几次来禀知县，说这凶器确是宋江的，必须拿宋江来审问，才有下落。
70 知县再三遮掩不住，只得差人去拿宋江。

[P38] 71 几个差人胡乱走了一转，便回说宋江在逃，不知去向。张文远又来禀道：‘宋江虽然逃去，可将他父宋太公及胞弟宋清拘来，要他们交出宋江。’知县只好又派人去宋家庄拘宋太公和宋清。
72 差人来到宋家庄，唤出太公，将文书给他看了。太公说：‘数年前我在县内告过他忤逆，出了他的籍，不在老汉户内人数。他本人行事与家中无涉。’他拿出执凭文帖，请公人抄了去向知县回话。

[P39] 73 知县看过文帖，正自高兴，不料那张三又挑唆阎婆上堂喊冤，说宋江是有名的孝子，谁个不知？那文帖是假的！说着哭哭啼啼，不肯罢休。
74 知县无可奈何，只得押了一纸公文，差朱仝、雷横两个都头带人到宋家庄再去搜捕宋江到案。朱仝、雷横领了公文，点起四十名士兵，径奔宋家庄。

[P40] 75 朱仝、雷横见过宋太公，说明来意。宋太公依然推说宋江已经出籍，从不回家。朱仝说是奉帖拘人，概不由己，要在庄上搜一搜。
76 朱仝把住门，叫四十名士兵围住庄院，由雷横去搜。雷横在庄前庄后搜了一遍，空手回来见朱仝，说宋江真的不在庄里。

[P41] 77 朱仝又叫雷横把住门，自己再去搜查。他进入庄里，把门拴了，一个人走进佛堂，把供桌拖在一边，揭起那片地板来。地底下有条绳子，把绳子一拉，铜铃便响起来。
78 听见铃响，宋江从地窖子里钻了出来，看见朱仝，吃了一惊。朱仝告诉他官司情形，并说因怕雷横固执，不会周全人，特地一个人来找他说话。宋江再三向他道谢。
哥哥往常曾和我说过你家有地窖，我猜想一定在此躲避。

[P42] 当行即行，
今晚便可动身，
切勿延误，官司
的事你可放心，
都任我身上。
79 朱仝和宋江一向要好，劝他及早出走。宋江说，有
三个安身之处：一是沧州横海郡柴进庄上；二是清风寨
花荣处；三是白虎山孔太公庄上。朱仝劝他速行。宋江
谢了朱仝，又入地窖去了。
80 朱仝出来对大家说宋江真没在庄里，又假意和雷横
商议要带走太公；雷横知道朱仝和宋江要好，猜他不是
真意，也乐得做个人情，不主张捉拿太公。

[P43] 81 宋太公叫人备下酒饭，众人吃罢回县里去了。
82 知县升堂，朱仝、雷横上来回话，说庄前庄后搜了两遍，并无宋江本人。宋太公卧病在床，他兄弟出外未归，都无法归案。知县听了，只好呈请本府，写一张海捕文书，也就算了。

[P44] 83 朱仝、雷横走后，宋江便准备和兄弟出外避难。当夜四更时分，兄弟两个收拾停当，父子三人洒泪而别。宋江兄弟出了宋家庄，径奔沧州横海郡小旋风柴进庄上而去。

后 记

下集是《狮子楼》。故事描绘的是：宋江避难到沧州柴进家中，结识武松；武松在景阳冈打死猛虎，被阳谷县起用当步兵都头。在阳谷县他遇见胞兄武大郎。武大郎妻潘金莲与恶霸西门庆私通，乘武松出差之时，毒死大郎；武松回来，查明此事，告状不准，就杀了潘金莲，又到狮子楼杀死西门庆，为哥哥报仇后自首，被判充军。

[P45] 宋 江 杀 惜

[P1] Song Jiang Kills Xi
Water Margin
Part Eight
Publishing Note
"Water Margin" is a classical Chinese literary masterpiece. To meet the needs of a wide readership, we have adapted it into a series of illustrated storybooks. In the adaptation, we have tried to preserve the original plot as much as possible, but some scenes have been slightly cut or modified to suit the format of illustrated stories.

The entire series consists of thirty volumes, each containing a relatively complete story that can stand alone; at the same time, the content of each volume connects with the previous and next, allowing for continuous reading. For convenience, each volume begins with a content summary and ends with a postscript, outlining the plot of the previous, current, and next volumes.

The "Water Margin" illustrated series was previously published by our publishing house between 1956 and 1962. This current set has been newly illustrated using the original literary script.

№ 000152

Volume 2: Lu Zhishen
Volume 3: The Wild Boar Forest
Volume 4: Lin Chong's Night Ascent to Liangshan
Volume 5: Yang Zhi Sells His Sword

Volume 14: Three Attacks on Zhu's Manor
Volume 15: Gaotang Prefecture
Volume 16: The Great Breakthrough of the Linked Horse Formation
Volume 17: The Gathering of the Three Mountains
Volume 18: The Riot at Huashan
Volume 19: The Great Name Prefecture
Volume 20: Zengtou City
Volume 21: Heroes Seating the Hierarchy
Volume 22: Li Kui Riots in Dongjing
Volume 23: Yan Qing Fights the Tournament
Volume 24: Black Whirlwind Tears the Imperial Edict
Volume 25: Two Breakthroughs Against Tong Guan
Volume 26: Three Defeats Against Gao Qiu
Volume 27: Accepting the Imperial Recruitment and Being Betrayed
Volume 28: Breaking the Liao Kingdom in Vain
Volume 29: Campaigning Against Fang La, Losing Troops and Generals
Volume 30: Liao'er Bay

Song Jiang Kills Xi
(The Water Margin, Volume 8)
Adapted by Qu Tan
Illustrated by Gao Shi
Scanned by Sidi Academy
Produced by Jin Ma Chao
People's Fine Arts Publishing House

[P3] Content Summary
The previous volume, "Shi Jie Village," tells of how Chao Gai and seven other heroes were caught after stealing the birthday tribute, but were warned in advance by Song Jiang and escaped to Shi Jie Village. When soldiers pursued them, the heroes killed all the soldiers and then fled to Liangshan; Wang伦 refused to take them in, so Lin Chong killed Wang伦, and Chao Gai became the leader of Liangshan.
This volume continues the story: Liangshan sent Liu Tang to deliver gold and a letter to Song Jiang. Song Jiang, in a moment of carelessness, left the bag containing the gold and letter at Yan Po Xi's place. Yan Po Xi discovered that Song Jiang had secret ties with Liangshan, seized the opportunity to blackmail him. Song Jiang killed Yan Po Xi in anger and fled to Cangzhou.
1 The soldiers of Jizhou were defeated twice by the heroes of Liangshan, which enraged Cai Jing, who dismissed the governor. After the new governor took office, he recruited soldiers, bought horses, stored grass and grain, and issued official documents to nearby prefectures and counties to jointly deal with Liangshan.

[P4] 2 The county of Yuncheng, under the jurisdiction of Jizhou Prefecture, received an official document from Jizhou. The county magistrate hurriedly summoned the clerk Song Jiang to draft the official notice and inform all villages. After reading the document, Song Jiang thought to himself: Chao Gai and the others, I never intended to commit such a great crime, which is a serious offense. Although they were forced by others, the law cannot forgive them. If there is any mistake, what can be done!
3 Song Jiang came out of the衙 (yé, official residence), walked onto the street, and heard someone behind him calling "clerk." When he turned around, he saw Wang Po, the matchmaker, leading a woman, pointing at him and talking.
You have good fortune, the clerk who does good deeds has arrived!

[P5] May the magistrate show mercy,
and grant a coffin!
4 Wang Po brought the woman to meet Song Jiang. The woman's surname was Yan, from Dongjing.
A family of three, they had come to Shandong to visit relatives but failed to find them, and ended up stranded here, relying solely on their daughter's singing for a living. Yesterday, her husband died of plague, and they had no money to bury him, leaving them utterly desperate...
Thank you, magistrate, for your great kindness!
5 Song Jiang agreed to provide a coffin. He immediately went to an inn, borrowed writing tools, and wrote a note instructing them to go to Chen Sanlang's house east of the county to collect it; he also gave the woman ten taels of silver to prepare for the funeral.

[P6] 6 A few days later, Yan Po came to thank Song Jiang. Seeing no woman in his room, she asked the neighbor Wang Po whether Song Jiang had a wife. Wang Po said no, and Yan Po then told Wang Po that she wanted to give her daughter, Po Xi, to Song Jiang as a concubine.
7 Wang Po told Song Jiang about this. Song Jiang initially refused, but couldn't withstand Wang Po's persuasion, and finally agreed.

[P7] 8 Song Jiang rented a house in the west alley of the county, bought some furniture, and settled down with Grandma Yan and her daughter Xiaoxi. Life was comfortable. However, Song Jiang was a man of integrity who loved practicing martial arts and, due to his busy official duties, rarely came home, which greatly displeased the woman.
9 One day, Song Jiang invited his fellow official Zhang Wenyuan to Grandma Yan's house for a drink. Zhang Wenyuan was a man of debauchery, nicknamed 'Little Zhang San,' but he was also handsome. As soon as Xiaoxi saw him, she was very pleased. The two exchanged glances and both developed feelings for each other.

[P8] 10 From then on, Zhang Wenyuan would sneak over whenever Song Jiang was away, pretending to look for him. The woman would invite him in for tea, and after talking and chatting, the two began to flirt and become involved.
11 The two of them met openly and secretly, growing increasingly close. As time passed, the neighbors found out and began to whisper and gossip behind their backs.

[P9] 12 Although some rumors reached Song Jiang's ears, he thought to himself: 'She is not my wife of many years; why bother with such trivial troubles? I'll just stop going to her house.' From then on, Song Jiang didn't visit for several months. Even when Yan Po sent someone to invite him, he always made excuses.
13 One evening, Song Jiang came out of the government office and went to the teahouse across the street for tea. Suddenly, he saw a big man, carrying a朴刀 (pǔdāo, a type of broadsword) and a bundle, sweating profusely as he walked straight toward the county office, looking inside.

[P10] 14 Song Jiang saw the big man coming suspiciously and hurried after him. He looked closely and felt the man looked familiar, but couldn't remember where he had seen him. The big man stopped and looked at Song Jiang, also recognizing him somewhat.
15 The big man went to a shop by the roadside to ask the shopkeeper. The shopkeeper told him, 'This is Officer Song.' The big man then stepped forward to greet him and asked Song Jiang to go to a quiet place to talk.

[P11] 16 Song Jiang and the big man sat down in a quiet corner of a wine pavilion. The big man leaned his broadsword, took off his bundle, threw it under the table, and bowed immediately.
17 Song Jiang hurriedly returned the courtesy. The big man said he was Liu Tang, the Red-Haired Ghost, sent by Chief Chao to personally thank his benefactor. Song Jiang asked about the situation at Liangshan, and Liu Tang explained it all.

[P12] You seven have just arrived at the mountain stronghold and are short on silver. My family can still manage, so there's no need to keep it all.
18 Liu Tang opened the bundle and took out a letter from Chao Gai and one hundred taels of gold, handing them to Song Jiang. After reading the letter, Song Jiang took one bar of gold and placed it with the letter in his official pouch, then told Liu Tang to take the rest back.
19 Liu Tang insisted that Song Jiang accept the gold, but Song Jiang firmly refused. He immediately took ink and paper and wrote a reply letter to Chao Gai. Liu Tang had no choice but to wrap the gold back into the bundle. Song Jiang then called the waiter to bring wine and meat for Liu Tang to eat.

[P13] Brother, take care. Don't come back again. There are many officials here; it's not a safe place.
20 It was already late. Song Jiang, fearing trouble, urged Liu Tang to return to the mountain stronghold immediately. Liu Tang took his leave, and Song Jiang saw him off to the alley entrance, then grabbed Liu Tang's hand and gave him a few final warnings.
Where are you going, Mr. Yansi? It's been two good days since we last met.
21 After Liu Tang left, Song Jiang walked back to his residence. As he walked, he thought to himself: Fortunately, the officials didn't see us. We almost caused a big incident! After turning two corners, he heard someone calling him from behind. He turned around and saw it was Yan Po again.

[P14] My child, your third husband is here!
23 Song Jiang, unable to resist the old woman's纠缠, had to go with her to Yan's house. The old woman dragged Song Jiang inside and hurriedly called for Po Xi to come down to greet him. The woman thought it was Zhang San who had arrived, and hurriedly got up, brushing her hair with her hands, and ran downstairs like a bird.
24 Po Xi, seeing from the window lattice that it was Song Jiang, turned back. The old woman, hearing that her daughter had gone back upstairs, said some kind words to Song Jiang and forcibly dragged him upstairs.

[P15] 25 Song Jiang felt very uncomfortable, as he was dragged by the old woman and couldn't escape, so he could only reluctantly go upstairs. Yan Poxi, however, lay in bed and refused to get up.
26 Song Jiang sat on a stool. Yan Po dragged her daughter and wanted her to come and accompany Song Jiang. The woman wouldn't agree, and although she was forced to sit next to Song Jiang, she turned her face away.
Look at how willful you are. You hurt him with your words every day, making the magistrate not come to the door, and yet you miss him. What is the point of this?

[P16] 27 Yan Po talked to herself for a while, then pretended to go downstairs to buy some fruits for wine, and left. Song Jiang tried to slip away, but unexpectedly, Yan Po locked the door from the outside.
28 Song Jiang had no choice but to sit down. Soon after, Yan Po brought up the wine, pleaded with them, and finally, everyone sat down to drink. Song Jiang had no choice but to pick up his cup and drank three or five cups...

[P17] 29 It is said that in Yuncheng County there was a man named Tang Niuer who sold fermented food. Because Song Jiang often helped him, whenever he heard of any official matters, he would rush to inform Song Jiang; when Song Jiang needed him, he never refused. That day, having lost money gambling, he went to look for Song Jiang.
30 Tang Niuer asked around the neighborhood and learned that Song Jiang had gone to Yan Po's house. He ran to Yan's house, saw the door was not locked, and entered by himself; he walked to the side of the staircase and heard only Yan Po's laughter upstairs.

[P18] 31 Tang Niuer crept quietly up the stairs, peeked inside, and saw Song Jiang and Yan Po Xi both bowed their heads in silence.
32 Tang Niuer slipped in and bowed to the three people. Seeing him arrive, Song Jiang thought of a way to escape, and gave Tang Niuer a quick signal with his lips. Tang Niuer understood clearly, and then made up a story to deceive Yan Po.
Could it be that there's an urgent case at the衙?
It's because of that matter this morning; the county magistrate is furious at the hall and has sent four or five constables to look for you everywhere.

[P19] Every word is true, and I have never lied.
You rogue, coming to deceive old woman, do you think you can fool me?
33 Song Jiang said, "This is urgent, I must go." He got up to go downstairs. Yan Po wouldn't let him, saying Tang Niuer was lying to deceive her. Tang Niuer argued with her, and Yan Po started arguing with him...
Why are you hitting me?
You ruin people's livelihoods, like killing their parents and wives!
34 The two argued more fiercely. The old woman jumped up, gave Tang Niuer a hard shove to the neck, stumbled, and rushed down the stairs from the room.

[P20] 35 Tang Niuer tried to rush toward Yan Po, but was struck twice across the face by Yan Po, who spread her fingers wide, causing him to fall all the way out the door. Yan Po shut the door and kept on cursing.
36 Tang Niuer stood outside the door, pounding his chest and stomping his feet, cursing loudly as he left.
You thief and pest! If it weren't for Song Yansi's sake, I'd make your house crumble to dust!

[P21] It's getting late,
You two should go to bed soon!
37 Yan Po went upstairs and scolded Tang Niuer in front of Song Jiang, making it even harder for Song Jiang to leave. The old woman then劝 him to drink a few more cups of wine and urged him to go to bed.
38 Song Jiang thought: It's late now, I can't leave anyway, let's see if this woman still has any feelings for me. After sitting for a while, he saw that the woman didn't even take off her clothes, but went straight to bed and turned over to sleep facing the inside.

[P22] 39 Song Jiang thought: How hateful, this woman pays me no attention at all! I can only sleep for a while for now, and leave as soon as possible tomorrow morning. He took off the belt from his waist, which held his official document pouch and a paper-cutting knife, hung it on the bed rail, and then lay down back-to-back with the woman.
40 Song Jiang felt depressed and couldn't sleep. He barely endured until dawn, then got up, washed his face with cold water from a basin, and walked downstairs.

[P23] Please, Sir, have a bowl of hot soup before you go.
41 Song Jiang left Yan's house and hurried back to his lodging, passing in front of the county office. He saw an old man selling hot noodle soup at the morning market. The old man called out to Song Jiang and handed him a bowl of sobering soup.
Ah!
42 Song Jiang took the soup and ate a few mouthfuls. He remembered he had once promised this old man a coffin. Now, he thought he could give him the gold sent by Chao Gai. He lifted his front robe to take the gold, but then realized his official document pouch was missing.

[P24] 43 Song Jiang was startled and thought to himself: This is terrible. If that woman gets hold of the document pouch and discovers the letter from Chao Gai inside, what will I do? He immediately turned around and walked back toward Yan Po's house.
44 Meanwhile, Yan Po Xi, having waited for Song Jiang to leave, wanted to get up, take off her clothes, and go back to sleep. She looked up and saw the purple silk ribbon hanging on the bed rail, so she casually picked it up.

[P25] Goodness, Song Jiang, Song Jiang! So you've been secretly communicating with Liangshan! Today you've fallen into my hands!
45 Yan Po-xi picked up the document bag and knife, felt it was heavy, and shook it onto the bed, revealing a packet of gold and a letter. This woman could read a few characters, so she looked at the letter by the lamp and exclaimed with delight.
46 Yan Po-xi was overjoyed, putting the letter, gold, and knife back into the document bag. At that moment, she heard the door downstairs creak, and guessed it must be Song Jiang returning. So she hid the phoenix belt and the document bag under the covers, pulled the blanket over herself, and pretended to be asleep.

[P26] 47 Song Jiang walked in and went straight to the bedpost to retrieve his bag, but it was gone. He was startled.
48 Song Jiang could only hold his breath and shook the woman with his hand, demanding his bag. Yan Po Xi pretended to be asleep and said nothing.
Sister, return my bag!

[P27] There's no one else here, it must be you who took it.
49 Song Jiang could only beg the woman, but she ignored him; he asked her again and again, but she said she hadn't seen it. Song Jiang grew desperate and said she must have hidden it.
Sister, don't shout, the neighbors will hear, and that won't be good.
Oh, so you're secretly communicating with bandits from Liangshan!
50 The woman, upon hearing Song Jiang accuse her of taking it, opened her eyes wide and said, "I did take it, but I won't give it back." Then she started shouting about "Liangshan this, Liangshan that." Song Jiang hurriedly begged her not to shout.

[P28] 51 Song Jiang pleaded for a long time. Ya Po Xi said, if he wanted to get back the document bag, he must agree to three things: first, let her marry Zhang San; second, all her clothes and belongings would belong to her; third, quickly hand over the one hundred taels of gold mentioned in Chao Gai's letter, all of it to her.
52 Song Jiang said he could agree to the first two, but he had only received ten taels of gold, and the rest had been taken by the messenger. The woman wouldn't believe him. Song Jiang had no choice but to beg for a three-day deadline to sell his property and raise one hundred taels of gold for her.

[P29] 53 The woman refused, insisting on a cash-and-delivery deal, and said that if that were the case, Song Jiang could come back in three days to retrieve the bag. Song Jiang pleaded desperately, but the woman grew angry and said: 'If you can't produce the gold today, I'll go to the court tomorrow to get the bag!'
54 Hearing the word 'court', Song Jiang's anger flared. He could no longer restrain himself and, without hesitation, grabbed the woman's blanket.
You really
won't return it?
I'll get it at the county衙
and return it to you!

[P30] 55 The woman, disregarding the blanket, clutched the document bag tightly. Song Jiang, seeing the bag right before her chest, rushed forward to seize it.
56 The woman refused to let go. Song Jiang pulled hard, drawing out the paper-cutting knife and gripping it firmly. The woman, thinking Song Jiang was about to attack, screamed desperately.
Black Third Brother: He's going to kill me!

[P31] 57 Song Jiang's pent-up anger had nowhere to go; after she screamed, he truly felt murderous. Just as the woman was about to scream again, Song Jiang grabbed her neck, raised the knife, and killed her.
58 Song Jiang killed Po Xi, quickly took the official bag, pulled out the letter, and burned it by the lamp.

[P32] Your daughter was so rude, I killed her.
What? That can't be true! You must be joking, Mr. Yansi.
59 Song Jiang adjusted his clothes and walked downstairs. Yan Po, hearing her daughter scream, rushed upstairs and collided with Song Jiang. Song Jiang then explained to Yan Po what had happened with the killing of Yan Po Xi.
60 Yan Po still didn't believe it. She ran into the room, gasped, and said, "The Yansi killed my daughter! How will I live now?" Song Jiang quickly reassured her, saying, "Don't worry, I'll take care of you."

[P33] 61 Yan Po pretended to agree, only asking Song Jiang to handle her daughter's funeral arrangements. Song Jiang wanted to write a note for Yan Po to go to Chen Sanlang's house to fetch a coffin, but Yan Po refused, insisting on going with Song Jiang. So Song Jiang and the old woman left together...
62 It was just dawn. Yan Po and Song Jiang passed by the county衙 gate. The gate had just opened, and the old woman, catching him off guard, grabbed Song Jiang and shouted loudly.
There's a murderer
Here!

[P34] Wife, let go! There's something to talk about, the magistrate is not such a person!
63 Song Jiang was panicked, trying to stop the old woman, but couldn't hold her. Soon, several constables came over. Seeing it was Song Jiang, they advised the woman to let him go. Since Song Jiang was usually a good man, respected by all, the constables didn't believe the woman's words and refused to arrest him on the spot.
Old thief,
what are you doing, grabbing the magistrate?
64 Just then, Tang Niuer came to sell fermented ginger. Seeing Yan Po grabbing Song Jiang and shouting, he remembered his anger from last night, rushed forward, pulled the woman's hand away, spread his fingers, and slapped Yan Po. Song Jiang took the opportunity to escape.

[P35] 65 Yan Po had no choice but to grab Tang Niuer and scream. The three or four constables, who had just refrained from acting out of respect for Song Jiang, now stepped forward and took the old woman and Tang Niuer into the county衙 gate.
66 The magistrate convened court. Yan Po accused Song Jiang of murdering her daughter and pointed to Tang Niuer, claiming he had instigated the crime last night and helped the murderer escape this morning. The magistrate, intending to exonerate Song Jiang, said Song Jiang was an honest gentleman who would never kill anyone, and thus the murder must have been committed by Tang Niuer.

[P36] 67 Tang Niuer said he did not know about the killing of Yan Po's daughter. The magistrate ignored him, ordered the clerks to take statements from everyone, and led the coroner, the village head, and others to Yan Po's house to examine the body and the weapon. This confirmed that the victim had indeed been murdered.
68 The magistrate, who intended to save Song Jiang, only interrogated Tang Niuer, did not allow him to defend himself, ordered the guards to bind and beat him severely, and then had a wooden collar placed on him, imprisoning him in jail.
I was just passing by to break up the fight; I truly did not know about the matter of Song Yansi killing someone.

[P37] 69 Unbeknownst to them, the case fell into Zhang Wenyuan's hands. He was determined to avenge Yan Po Xi, so he took the weapon and repeatedly reported to the magistrate, claiming the weapon was indeed Song Jiang's, and that Song Jiang must be brought in for questioning to resolve the matter.
70 The magistrate could no longer conceal the truth and had no choice but to send someone to arrest Song Jiang.

[P38] 71 A few constables wandered around aimlessly and returned to report that Song Jiang had fled, with no known whereabouts. Zhang Wenyuan then reported: 'Although Song Jiang has escaped, you should arrest his father, Song Taigong, and his younger brother, Song Qing, and force them to hand over Song Jiang.' The magistrate had no choice but to send people again to Songjiazhuang to arrest Song Taigong and Song Qing.
72 The constables arrived at Songjiazhuang, summoned the elder, and showed him the document. The elder said: 'Years ago, I reported him for filial disobedience to the county, removed him from my household register, and he is no longer counted among my family members. His actions have nothing to do with our household.' He then produced a formal document and asked the constables to copy it and return to the magistrate with the reply.

[P39] 73 The magistrate had just seen the document and was pleased, but unexpectedly, Zhang San incited Yan Po to cry out for justice in court, saying Song Jiang was a well-known filial son—how could anyone not know? The document was fake! She cried and sobbed, refusing to stop.
74 The magistrate, having no choice, issued an official document and sent Zhu Tong and Lei Heng, two head constables, with men to Songjia Zhuang to search for and capture Song Jiang. Zhu Tong and Lei Heng received the document, gathered forty soldiers, and hurried straight to Songjia Zhuang.

[P40] 75 Zhu Tong and Lei Heng met Song Taigong and explained their purpose. Song Taigong still insisted that Song Jiang had already left the household register and never returned home. Zhu Tong said he was acting on an official order and had no choice but to search the estate.
76 Zhu Tong blocked the gate and called forty soldiers to surround the courtyard, sending Lei Heng to search. Lei Heng searched the front and back of the estate, returned empty-handed to Zhu Tong, and reported that Song Jiang was truly not in the house.

[P41] 77 Zhu Tong called Lei Heng to guard the door and went to search himself. He entered the estate, locked the door, walked into the Buddhist hall alone, dragged the altar aside, and lifted a floorboard. There was a rope underneath; when he pulled it, a bronze bell rang.
78 Hearing the bell, Song Jiang crawled out of the cellar and saw Zhu Tong, startled. Zhu Tong told him about the legal situation and explained that he had come alone to speak with him, fearing Lei Heng's stubbornness and inability to be considerate. Song Jiang repeatedly thanked him.
Brother, you once told me your house had a cellar; I guessed you must be hiding here.

[P42] Act now, set out tonight,
Do not delay, you can rest assured about the official matter,
It's all on me.
79 Zhu Tong and Song Jiang have always been close friends, and he urged him to leave early. Song Jiang said he had three places to hide: first, at Chai Jin's estate in Henghai Prefecture, Cangzhou; second, at Hua Rong's place in Qingfeng Fort; third, at Kong Taigong's estate on Baihu Mountain. Zhu Tong urged him to leave quickly. Song Jiang thanked Zhu Tong and went back into the cellar.
80 Zhu Tong came out and told everyone that Song Jiang was truly not in the village, then pretended to discuss with Lei Heng about taking away Song Taigong; Lei Heng, knowing that Zhu Tong was close to Song Jiang, guessed he was not serious, and was happy to do him a favor, so he did not insist on arresting Song Taigong.

[P43] 81 Song Taigong had wine and food prepared, and after everyone finished eating, they returned to the county.
82 The magistrate ascended the hall, and Zhu Tong and Lei Heng reported back, saying they had searched the front and back of the estate twice, but found no trace of Song Jiang. Song Taigong was ill in bed, and his brother was away and had not returned, so they could not be brought to justice. Upon hearing this, the magistrate could only submit a request to the prefectural office to issue a wanted notice, and that would be the end of it.

[P44] 83 After Zhu Tong and Lei Heng left, Song Jiang prepared to flee with his brothers. At the fourth watch of the night, the two brothers had everything packed, and the three of them parted with tears. Song Jiang and his brother left Song's village and hurried to the residence of Chai Jin, the 'Little Whirlwind,' in Cangzhou, Henghai Prefecture.

Postscript

The next episode is 'Lion's Den.' The story depicts: Song Jiang takes refuge at Chai Jin's home in Cangzhou and meets Wu Song; Wu Song kills a tiger on Jingyang Ridge and is appointed as a foot soldier captain by Yanggu County. In Yanggu, he meets his elder brother Wu Dalang. Wu Dalang's wife Pan Jinlian has an affair with the bully Xi Men Qing, and while Wu Song is away on duty, she poisons Dalang; when Wu Song returns, he investigates, finds the truth, but his complaint is rejected, so he kills Pan Jinlian, then goes to Lion's Den to kill Xi Men Qing, avenges his brother, surrenders himself, and is sentenced to military exile.

[P1] 本页为连环画《水浒》之八《宋江杀惜》的封面及出版说明。封面描绘了宋江持刀面对床上女子的场景，出版说明介绍了该连环画册的改编原则、结构和出版背景。
[P2] 本页为连环画《水浒》之八《宋江杀惜》的目录页，列出了全系列三十集的标题，并注明了本册的改编者、绘者、扫描者、制作者及出版社。
[P3] 本页为连环画《水浒》之八《宋江杀惜》的内容提要，回顾了上集《石碣村》的剧情，并介绍了本集宋江因疏忽将梁山来信遗落在阎婆惜处，被其要挟后怒杀阎婆惜并逃往沧州的故事梗概。下方插图及文字描述了济州官兵败于梁山后，新知府准备联合围剿梁山的情节。
[P4] 本页描绘了宋江收到济州公文后内心的挣扎，以及他从衙门出来后被王婆等人认出并打招呼的场景。
[P5] 本页描绘了王婆带阎婆到宋江处求助，因阎婆丈夫病逝无钱安葬，宋江答应施舍棺材并给予银两，随后在酒店写下取棺凭据。
[P6] 本页描绘了阎婆因宋江无妻室，通过王婆向其提亲，欲将女儿婆惜许配给宋江；宋江起初拒绝，后经王婆劝说同意。画面分为两格，分别表现阎婆与王婆交谈及王婆向宋江说媒的场景。
[P7] 本页描绘了宋江为阎婆惜母女租屋安顿，但因公务繁忙少回家，导致阎婆惜不满；随后宋江请同僚张文远到家中饮酒，张文远与阎婆惜一见钟情，暗生情愫。
[P8] 本页描绘了张文远趁宋江不在家时与阎婆惜秘密往来，两人逐渐勾搭成奸，关系日益亲密，街坊邻居也逐渐知晓并私下议论。
[P9] 本页描述了宋江得知阎婆惜与张文远私通后，选择回避并疏远她，此后数月未去其家；另一场景中，宋江在茶坊喝茶时，见到一名持刀背包袱的大汉正朝县衙方向走去。
[P10] 宋江在街上遇见一名行迹可疑的大汉，两人互相认出对方，大汉随后向掌柜打听确认宋江身份，并上前招呼，邀请他到僻静处谈话。
[P11] 宋江与自称赤发鬼刘唐的大汉在酒楼僻静处会面，刘唐奉晁盖之命前来感谢宋江，并向他详细讲述了梁山的情况。
[P12] 刘唐将晁盖的信和一百两黄金交给宋江，宋江只收下一条金子并回信，其余金子让刘唐带回；随后宋江请刘唐饮酒。
[P13] 宋江送别刘唐后，担心事情败露，心有余悸；返回途中，被阎婆叫住，暗示两人关系未断。
[P14] 宋江被阎婆强行带到阎家，阎婆惜误以为是张文远到来，匆忙下楼迎接，但发现是宋江后又转身回楼；阎婆见状便对宋江说好话，强行将他拖上楼。
[P15] 宋江被阎婆强行拖上楼，内心不自在；阎婆逼迫女儿阎婆惜陪宋江，但阎婆惜不愿，只肯坐于一旁并转过脸去，阎婆则责备她任性。
[P16] 阎婆借口买果品下楼，趁机锁门，宋江无法脱身；随后阎婆端酒上楼，强行劝宋江饮酒，宋江只得勉强饮下几杯。
[P17] 唐牛儿因赌输钱去找宋江，得知宋江在阎婆家后，便潜入阎家，听到楼上只有阎婆一人说笑。
[P18] 唐牛儿潜入阎婆家，发现宋江与阎婆惜低头无语，便趁机编造知县派人找宋江的谎言，帮助宋江脱身。
[P19] 宋江在唐牛儿的帮助下试图离开阎婆家，阎婆不允并与其争辩，唐牛儿与阎婆争吵，阎婆恼羞成怒，推搡唐牛儿并冲下楼去。
[P20] 唐牛儿试图帮助宋江脱身，被阎婆打出门外；阎婆关上门继续骂人，唐牛儿在门外愤怒地大骂后离开。
[P21] 阎婆上楼后继续责骂唐牛儿，迫使宋江无法脱身，并劝其饮酒安歇；宋江无奈，见阎婆惜不脱衣裳便上床背对而睡，心中犹豫是否还有情分。
[P22] 宋江因被阎婆惜冷落而心生怨恨，无奈之下与她背靠背睡下，并将招文袋和尖刀挂在床栏上；次日五更，他因气闷无法安睡，起身洗脸后走下楼去。
[P23] 宋江离开阎婆家后，在县衙前遇到卖热汤的王老汉，对方递给他一碗醒酒汤。宋江喝汤时想起曾许诺给老汉一口棺材，便想取出晁盖送的金子，却发现随身携带的招文袋不见了。
[P24] 宋江发现招文袋不见后惊觉危险，立即返回阎婆家；阎婆惜则在宋江离开后，发现床栏上的紫罗鸾带并顺手取走。
[P25] 阎婆惜发现宋江的招文袋中藏有金子和书信，识得字后大喜，将物品重新装袋；她听到楼下动静，以为宋江归来，便将招文袋和鸾带藏于被下，假装睡觉。
[P26] 宋江返回阎婆惜家中，发现招文袋不见，惊觉不妙；他摇醒假装睡觉的阎婆惜，要求归还招文袋，但对方装睡不回应。
[P27] 宋江发现招文袋不见后，向阎婆惜讨要，对方假装睡觉不理，宋江急切质问，阎婆惜醒来后承认拿走但拒绝归还，并开始大喊宋江私通梁山贼人，宋江连忙劝阻她不要嚷叫。
[P28] 宋江向阎婆惜讨回招文袋，对方提出三个条件：改嫁张三、所有财物归她、交出晁盖信中的一百两金子。宋江同意前两项，但称金子只收到十两，其余被送信人带走，请求三天时间变卖家产凑齐金子。
[P29] 阎婆惜拒绝宋江的延期请求，要求立即交钱并威胁若不给金子就去公堂取招文袋；宋江听后怒不可遏，动手扯开她的被子。
[P30] 宋江与阎婆惜为争夺招文袋发生激烈拉扯，宋江拉出裁纸刀，阎婆惜误以为他要行凶，惊恐大叫。
[P31] 宋江在阎婆惜第二次欲喊叫时将其杀死，随后取回招文袋并烧毁了晁盖的信件。
[P32] 宋江杀死阎婆惜后下楼，阎婆闻声上楼，宋江向其说明情况；阎婆不信，进房后见女儿已死，悲痛欲绝，宋江承诺由他赡养。
[P33] 阎婆与宋江一同出门，准备处理女儿后事；路过县衙时，阎婆突然扭住宋江并大喊抓贼，引发骚动。
[P34] 阎婆在县衙前扭住宋江喊抓贼，公差因宋江平日为人好而不信其言，未予抓捕；恰逢唐牛儿路过，因昨日积怨上前将阎婆推开并打了一巴掌，宋江趁机逃脱。
[P35] 阎婆抓住唐牛儿喊叫，公差将二人带入县衙；知县升堂审理，阎婆指控宋江杀人并牵连唐牛儿，知县有意开脱宋江，将罪责归于唐牛儿。
[P36] 知县不采信唐牛儿的辩解，命人验尸确认死者被杀，随后为救宋江，将唐牛儿严刑拷打并关入大牢。
[P37] 张文远得到案件后，为替阎婆惜报仇，多次向知县举报凶器属宋江，要求缉拿宋江；知县无法再隐瞒，只得派人去捉拿宋江。
[P38] 差人未能找到宋江，张文远建议抓捕其父宋太公和弟弟宋清；差人到宋家庄后，宋太公出示文书，声称宋江已脱离其户籍，与家中无关，要求公人将文书带回知县。
[P39] 阎婆在县衙上堂喊冤，声称宋江是孝子且文帖是假的，知县无奈只得派朱仝、雷横带兵前往宋家庄搜捕宋江。
[P40] 朱仝和雷横奉命到宋家庄搜捕宋江，宋太公称宋江已脱离户籍不在家，朱仝坚持搜查，雷横搜遍庄院后确认宋江不在家中。
[P41] 朱仝独自搜查宋家庄，在佛堂地板下发现机关并拉动绳索引发铜铃响动；宋江听见铃声从地窖钻出，朱仝告知官府情况并解释自己单独前来，宋江向他再三道谢。
[P42] 朱仝劝宋江立即出逃，并告知三个安身之处，宋江谢过朱仝后再次躲入地窖。朱仝对外宣称宋江不在庄中，并假意与雷横商议带走宋太公，雷横识破其意图，未主张捉拿宋太公。
[P43] 宋太公设宴款待朱仝、雷横等人，众人用餐后返回县衙。朱仝、雷横向知县汇报搜捕结果，称未找到宋江，宋太公卧病且其弟外出，无法归案，知县只得请求上级发布海捕文书。
[P44] 朱仝和雷横离开后，宋江与兄弟收拾行装，与父亲洒泪告别，连夜逃往沧州柴进庄上避难。页面下方的后记预告了下一集《狮子楼》的故事梗概，讲述武松打虎、为兄报仇的情节。
[P45] 本页为绘本《宋江杀惜》的版权页，列出了原著作者、改编者、绘者、出版发行信息、印刷信息及定价等。
